title: Open-Source Miniature Fluorimeter to Monitor Real-Time Isothermal Nucleic Acid Amplification Reactions in Resource-Limited Settings
protocol: 3D print the CAD files provided as Supplemental Files 1, 2, and 3 respectively for the first configuration.
3D print the CAD files provided as Supplemental Files 3, 4, and 5 respectively for the second configuration.
Prepare two light-to-digital sensor evaluation modules for parallel monitoring of two samples.
Remove R4 resistor on one of the sensor test boards.
Solder a jumper wire from the right pad of the R4 area to the top pad in the R1 area on the PCB.
Solder wires to each of the two Light Emitting Diodes (LEDs).
Connect a red wire (positive) to the pad labeled "1" on the LED and a black wire (negative) on the pad labeled "2" on the LED.
Apply a thin layer of thermal adhesive on the back of the LED.
Place the LED on the top of an end cap.
Wait until the thermal adhesive cures.
Add a heat sink to the other side of the end cap.
Insert the sensor test board into the top cavity of the housing.
Secure the sensor test board with a 3/16-inch-long 4-40 screw through the hole on the board.
Place one 20 mm focal length lens in the section below the sensor test board, convex side down.
Place the long pass filter into the next section below the lens for the first configuration.
Place two yellow emission filter foils into the section below the lens for the second configuration.
Place the dichroic mirror into the diagonal section near the center of the encasement following the manufacturer's orientation for the first configuration.
Place the beam splitter into the diagonal section for the second configuration, with no specific orientation needed.
Place a second 20 mm focal length lens into the section below the dichroic mirror (or beam splitter), convex side up.
Place the excitation filter in the section to the right of the dichroic mirror.
Ensure the arrow on the excitation filter points towards the dichroic mirror.
Insert one blue excitation filter foil into the section to the right of the beam splitter for the second configuration.
Place a 15 mm focal length lens to the right of the excitation filter, with the convex side facing the dichroic mirror.
Insert an LED into the remaining section of the print, ensuring it faces towards the dichroic mirror (or beam splitter).
Route the two wires from the LED into the recessed channels for a tight closure.
Repeat steps 2.3 to 2.9 for the other side of the 3D printed part.
Close the empty side of the print on top of the optical components assembly.
Insert the extruded portions of the top half of the encasement into the recessed grooves of the bottom half.
Secure the two halves together with 3/8-inch-long 4-40 screws.
Connect the two mini breadboards together.
Place the microcontroller onto one of the breadboards with the microUSB port facing outwards.
Connect the CTL pin of the LED (+) driver to a digital pin of the microcontroller.
Connect the LED (-) pin of the LED driver to a GND pin of the microcontroller.
Remove the plastic covers on the back of the breadboards.
Press the adhesive backing of the breadboards to attach them to the 3D printed part inside the back portion of the 'LCD_Screen_Holder.stl' printed part.
Secure the LCD screen holder with the assembled breadboards inside to the optical enclosure using one-inch-long 4-40 screws.
Connect the LED (+) pin of the LED driver to the positive wire of the first LED.
Connect the negative wire of the first LED to the positive wire of the second LED on the breadboard.
Connect the negative wire of the second LED to the LED (-) pin of the LED driver.
Connect the positive and negative wires of the 10 V power supply to the VIN+ and VIN- pins of the LED driver, respectively.
Connect the sensor test board power supply and data transfer.
Take a 4-pin female to male jumper wire.
Connect SCK, SDA, VDUT, and GND pins on the light-to-digital sensor test boards to the mini breadboard through the gap in the top right of the LCD Holder print.
Ensure connections between the 3.3 V pin of the microcontroller and the VDUT pin of both test boards.
Ensure connections between the GND pin of the microcontroller and the GND pin of both test boards.
Ensure connections between the analog 4 (A4) pin of the microcontroller and the SDA pin of both test boards.
Ensure connections between the analog 5 (A5) pin of the microcontroller and the SCK pin of both test boards.
Secure the single-board computer onto the LCD Screen holder with four M2.5 screws.
Connect the HDMI port of the single-board computer to the touchscreen's HDMI port.
Connect the touchscreen display to the single-board computer as per the touchscreen instructions.
Install and use the web editor to upload the custom sketch "MiniFluorimeter_2Diode.ino".
Ensure the "ClosedCube OPT3002" library is installed using the Library Manager.
Change the variable led_A_pin to the number of the digital pin used in step 3.3.
Adjust the value of the variable ExposureTime to change the duration the LED is turned on.
Adjust the value of the variable led_A_Interval to set milliseconds between LED exposures.
Change the variable led_Power to a number between zero and one for adjusting LED brightness during exposures.
Turn on touchscreen control capability following manufacturer's instructions provided with the 3.5-inch display.
Download the "MiniFluorimeter_2Diode_GUI.py" file from Supplemental Coding File 2.
Upload the downloaded GUI file to a desired location on the single-board computer.
Install a working version of Python on the single-board computer.
Install necessary libraries for the Python program.
Set measurement_time to the desired duration for data acquisition.
Specify serialPort variable with the address of the connected microcontroller.
Turn on the commercial heat block and wait for it to reach the desired temperature.
Power the single-board computer using a standard 5 V power supply.
Connect the single-board computer to the microcontroller via a microUSB to USB cable.
Open the provided Python script using the touchscreen interface.
Set outputFilepath to the name of the data file, ensuring it ends with '.xlsx'.
Place two PCR tubes containing reactions into the heat block.
Ensure alignment between the PCR tube positions and fluorimeter optical channels.
Place the fluorimeter atop the heat block with the PCR tubes centered between the pegs.
Ensure that the 3D printed fluorimeter is securely attached into the wells of the heat block.
Plug in the power supply adapter for the LEDs.
Use the touchscreen to start the Python program.
Observe real-time fluorescence measurements on the GUI for both PCR tubes.
After the experiment time has elapsed, acquisition ceases automatically.
View the measurements in the output data file saved in the user-defined location.
To end the measurements early, click the "Stop Acquisition" button on the user interface.
